newsitem.title: USA: CINAR Films mulls programming purchase.
newsitem.headline: CINAR Films mulls programming purchase.

text.p: CINAR Films Inc President Ronald Weinberg said the company is considering completing acquisition of a film production company over the next month that could raise the number of titles in its library to more than 1,000 by the end of 1996.

Weinberg told investors in a presentation to a Montgomery Securities conference here that the process could result in an acquisition "within the next month that would substantially increase our library to 1,000 half-hours by year end."
He declined to elaborate on the acquisition target, except to say it currently has a library of some 200 programs.

CINAR executives said the Montreal-based company itself, which specializes in non-violent children's television programs, expects to have added 170 half-hours through its own productions in 1996, raising its library to around 750.

CINAR may add to its educational side with an acquisition next year, Weinberg added. The company's core strategy is to focus on original programming, retain rights to these programs, seek partnerships with distribution channels and production companies and reduce financial risk via pre-sales and co-production.

Company executives noted that international sales have risen and that library sales, at $9.0 million in 1995, accounted for some 21.5 percent of its business, providing steady longer-term revenue streams and strong margins.
